fourviere.name: Notre-Dame de Fourvière
fourviere.slogan: A white basilica watching over two rivers and a million roofs.
fourviere.line: Lyonnais call it the upside-down elephant; it was built between 1872 and 1884 to a design by Pierre Bossan.

longuetraboule.name: Traboules of Vieux Lyon
longuetraboule.slogan: Secret passages through courtyards, from one street to the next.
longuetraboule.line: Lyon's first traboules are thought to date from the fourth century, when residents moved toward the Saône; silk workers later used them as shortcuts.

hallesbocuse.name: Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse
hallesbocuse.slogan: Sixty stalls where Lyon shops, snacks and argues about dinner.
hallesbocuse.line: Opened in 1971 to replace the Cordeliers market, the halls were renamed after chef Paul Bocuse in 2007.

perouges.name: Pérouges
perouges.slogan: Cobbled lanes so unspoiled that film crews keep coming back.
perouges.line: In the 19th century its population fell from 1,500 to 90, before restoration began in 1911.

brou.name: Royal Monastery of Brou
brou.slogan: A Flamboyant Gothic love letter carved in white marble.
brou.line: Margaret of Austria built it from 1506 to 1532 as the burial place for her husband, Philibert II of Savoy, who died at 24.
